title: What makes the lub-dub sound of a heartbeat
examples: Why does the heart go lub-dub?
What can you hear with a stethoscope?

explain.say: A heartbeat is a sequence that repeats about once a second. It starts with an electrical spark and ends with two valve sounds, lub and dub.

draw.text: What makes the lub-dub sound of a heartbeat

explain.say: The spark comes from the sinoatrial node, a patch of pacemaker cells in the right atrium. The signal spreads across the top rooms, which squeeze extra blood down into the ventricles.

stages.label: Atria squeeze
stages.note: Top rooms top up the ventricles

stages.label: Blood rushes out
stages.note: Into the lungs and the aorta

explain.say: After a short delay the ventricles squeeze. The rising pressure slams the inlet valves shut, and that closing makes the first, longer sound: lub.

stages.label: Atria squeeze
stages.note: Top rooms top up the ventricles

stages.label: Blood rushes out
stages.note: Into the lungs and the aorta

explain.say: Blood rushes out to the lungs and body. Then the ventricles relax, blood falls back against the exit valves, and they snap shut with the shorter second sound: dub.

faq.a: Lub is the sound of the tricuspid and mitral valves snapping shut when the ventricles start to squeeze. The blood and heart wall vibrate as the valves close.
asks: Why does the heart go lub?
What is the first heart sound?

faq.a: A small patch of special muscle cells in the right atrium, called the sinoatrial node, fires an electrical signal on its own about 60 to 100 times a minute at rest. That signal spreads through the heart and makes it squeeze.
asks: Tell me about the spark in the SA node

faq.a: Dub is the aortic and pulmonary valves closing at the end of the squeeze, when blood in the big arteries tries to fall back into the relaxed ventricles.
asks: What is the second heart sound?
Why does the heart go dub?

faq.q: Does the heart need the brain to beat?
faq.a: No. The heart makes its own electrical beat. Nerves and hormones such as adrenaline can speed it up or slow it down, but the rhythm itself starts in the heart.
asks: Can the heart beat on its own?

faq.q: Why is there a pause between beats?
faq.a: After each squeeze the heart muscle relaxes so the chambers can refill with blood. In a resting heart this filling time is longer than the squeeze itself.
asks: Why does the heart rest between beats?

facts: The first heart sound comes from the mitral and tricuspid valves closing; the second from the aortic and pulmonary valves closing.
The sinoatrial node in the right atrium is the heart's natural pacemaker.
A resting adult heart usually beats about 60 to 100 times a minute.
